fullPassage:
Art & Our Environment

While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings. That is why art has played an essential role in addressing social and global issues throughout history. Let us take a look at a few modern artworks that address environmental issues.

The first art piece is a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong. His artworks rally people around environmental actions. In the photo on the left, titled Turn Off the Plastic Tap, he tries to highlight the fact that a huge amount of plastic enters the ocean every minute.

He says, "You can't order a product online without having it delivered in plastic packaging. Also, the clothes you are wearing must be, at least in part, made of plastic. Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to opt out. Of course, you can choose not to purchase products containing plastic, but that only goes so far. I think it is important for you to inform your friends and family of the issue because at the end of the day, you know, companies and governments can't ignore the interest of the consumers. At the same time, we also need to pressure governments and corporations to do the right thing."

The next piece, titled Forget Me Not, is Jenny Kendler's personal love letter to the sea. She covered an old boom box with various shells, which took her a year to collect. The boom box plays something you may regard as calming ocean sounds. They are actually what she recorded as she had one of her baby teeth dissolve in acid. She wanted us to think of what sea creatures might go through one day if we continue burning fossil fuels carelessly. As the ocean absorbs more and more carbon dioxide, it becomes more and more acidic. Under this condition, the hard shells of many marine species will dissolve.

Kendler says, "I wanted to inspire people to raise their own awareness about what they can actually do as individuals, but at the same time, I hoped to encourage collective action and collective responsibility. One thing that art can do really well is to help us imagine how the world might be otherwise. Certainly, we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it."

The piece below, titled Homestead, is a painting by Jon Ching. Most of his work, including this painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet appeal to humans to appreciate the world around them. "I believe we've separated ourselves from nature and no longer see how we fit in. Instead of helping nature thrive, we are simply consuming it," says Ching.

One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun aspects of his work is how he blends the features of one life form with those of another. "I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in. I find it necessary to express a silver lining rather than just reflect on what's wrong. I want to show that everything is connected and that protecting nature is actually protecting us. My call to action is to remember the magic and wonder of this planet."

Art can strike up conversations about the environment, but more importantly, it can also make a great difference by inspiring us to take action. The following words from Andy Warhol, an American pop artist, ring especially true in this context. "They always say time changes things, but you actually have to change them yourself."

Banksy's New Work in Port Talbot

Secretive street artist Banksy designed another interesting piece of art, which appears on a concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales. It shows a child catching snowflakes with his mouth. When you look around the corner, however, you realize that the child's mouth is open to ash coming from a dumpster fire.

Banksy was asked by Gary Owen, a Port Talbot resident, to create art that would highlight Port Talbot's dust problem. Owen believed that the area's children were facing serious health risks by playing in the dust coming from the local steel plant.

Children are particularly defenseless against air pollution. Since they have faster breathing rates than adults, they breathe in more pollutants. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), about 93% of the world's children under 15 breathe in toxic air every day. In 2016, the WHO even estimated that about 600,000 children died from exposure to polluted air.

Banksy's art has included environmental messages before. For example, his 2010 artwork was created at the remains of a plant in Detroit. It showed a child with a can of red paint and the words, "I remember when all this was trees."

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis: ❌ ① playing → played: 'has played'(현재완료). has + p.p. 구조에서 과거분사 played 필요. playing(현재분사)은 불가. ✅ ② highlight: tries to + 동사원형. ✅ ③ enters: a huge amount of plastic(단수 취급) + enters. ✅ ④ finds: the individual consumer(3인칭 단수) + finds.
det.tip: 현재완료: has + p.p.(과거분사). has played (O) / has playing (X). play-played-played.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그것들을 모으는 데 1년이 ①걸렸다. 유치가 산에 ②녹게 했다. 바다 생물이 ③겪을 수 있는 일. 바다가 ④흡수하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① took: 'It took her a year to collect'. take-took-taken. ❌ ② dissolving → dissolve: 'had + O + 동사원형'. 사역동사 have는 목적보어로 원형부정사. dissolving(현재분사)이 아닌 dissolve(원형)가 맞음. ✅ ③ what: 'think of what ~' 간접의문문. ✅ ④ absorbs: the ocean(3인칭 단수) + absorbs.
det.tip: 사역동사 have + 목적어 + 동사원형: had her baby teeth dissolve (O) / dissolving (X).

questions.passage: I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems ①<u>which</u> I'm heavily interested in. det.korean: 깊이 관심을 두는 사안 ①에 대해. ②표출하는 것이 필요하다. 자연을 ③보호하는 것이. 행동을 취하도록 고무함으로써 ④~.
det.analysis: ✅ ① which: 관계대명사. interested in의 목적어. 전치사 뒤 which 가능. ✅ ② to express: find it necessary to V. 가목적어 구문. ✅ ③ protecting: 동명사 주어. protecting nature = 자연을 보호하는 것. ❌ ④ inspire → inspiring: 'by + V-ing'. 전치사 by 뒤 동명사 필요.
det.tip: by + V-ing(~함으로써): by inspiring (O) / by inspire (X). 전치사 뒤에는 동명사.

An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings. His artworks ②<u>rally</u> people around environmental actions. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ①격렬한 반응. 사람들을 ②집결시키다. 엄청난 ③양의 플라스틱. 1년 동안 ④배포하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① spirited: 원문 그대로. 격렬한. ✅ ② rally: 원문 그대로. 집결시키다. ✅ ③ amount: 원문 그대로. a huge amount of. ❌ ④ distribute → collect: 조개껍질을 '모으다'가 원문. distribute(배포하다)는 반대 방향.
det.tip: collect(모으다) ↔ distribute(배포하다, 분배하다). 조개껍질을 모으는 데 1년이 걸렸다.

questions.passage: I wanted to inspire people to raise their own awareness about what they can actually do as individuals, but at the same time, I hoped to encourage ①<u>collective</u> action and collective responsibility. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ①공동의 행동. 세상을 ②상상하다. 조용한 ③호소. 자연이 ④쇠퇴하도록.
det.analysis: ✅ ① collective: 원문 그대로. 공동의. ✅ ② imagine: 원문 그대로. 상상하다. ✅ ③ appeal: 원문 그대로. 호소. ❌ ④ decline → thrive: 원문은 'helping nature thrive'(자연이 번성하도록 돕다). decline(쇠퇴하다)는 반의어.
det.tip: thrive(번성하다) ↔ decline(쇠퇴하다). 'Instead of helping nature thrive' = 자연이 번성하도록 돕는 대신.

questions.passage: You can't order a product online without having it delivered in plastic packaging. Also, the clothes you are wearing must be, at least in part, made of plastic. Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to opt out. questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
According to Von Wong, the fundamental problem is that __________.
ch: consumers prefer plastic products over alternatives
dependence on plastic is embedded in the entire supply system
governments have banned the use of plastic materials
online shopping has become less popular recently

det.korean: 플라스틱에 대한 의존이 전체 공급 시스템에 내재되어 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain' 원문 직접 반영. embedded = built into. ❌ ①: 선호한다는 내용 없음. ❌ ③: 금지 — 반대 내용. ❌ ④: 인기 감소 — 언급 없음.
det.tip: built into = embedded in = '내재되어 있다'. supply chain = supply system = '공급망'.

questions.passage: I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in. I find it necessary to express a silver lining rather than just reflect on what's wrong. I want to show that everything is connected and that protecting nature is actually protecting us. My call to action is to remember the magic and wonder of this planet.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Jon Ching's artistic philosophy centers on the belief that __________.
ch: nature and humanity are fundamentally interconnected
art should focus exclusively on negative realities
individual artistic expression is more important than social impact
environmental problems cannot be solved through art

det.korean: 자연과 인류는 근본적으로 상호 연결되어 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: 'everything is connected' + 'protecting nature is actually protecting us'. 자연 보호 = 인간 보호라는 상호 연결성. ❌ ②: 부정적 현실에만 집중 — silver lining 표현과 반대. ❌ ③: 개인적 표현 > 사회적 영향 — 언급 없음. ❌ ④: 예술로 해결 불가 — 반대 입장.
det.tip: interconnected = connected. protecting nature = protecting us는 상호 연결의 핵심 메시지.

questions.passage: While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings. That is why art has played an essential role in addressing social and global issues throughout history. The first art piece is a photograph by Benjamin Von Wong. His artworks rally people around environmental actions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 예술은 역사 전반에 걸쳐 사회 문제를 다루는 역할을 해 왔다.
Von Wong의 작품은 경제 문제를 다룬다.

det.korean: 예술은 역사 전반에 걸쳐 사회와 세계의 문제점들을 다루는 데 중요한 역할을 해 왔다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 'art has played an essential role in addressing social and global issues throughout history'. ❌ ①: 아름다움뿐 아니라 spirited reaction도 끌어냄. ❌ ②: photographer(사진가). ❌ ④: environmental(환경) 문제.
det.tip: 선지의 축소/왜곡에 주의. '아름다움만' → '아름다움과 반응 둘 다'.

questions.passage: The next piece, titled Forget Me Not, is Jenny Kendler's personal love letter to the sea. She covered an old boom box with various shells, which took her a year to collect. She wanted us to think of what sea creatures might go through one day if we continue burning fossil fuels carelessly. As the ocean absorbs more and more carbon dioxide, it becomes more and more acidic. Under this condition, the hard shells of many marine species will dissolve.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Jenny Kendler의 작품 제목은 Remember Me이다.
바다가 이산화 탄소를 흡수하면 점점 더 산성이 된다.
Jenny Kendler는 조개껍질을 한 달 만에 모았다.
산성 조건에서 해양 생물의 껍질은 더 단단해진다.

det.korean: 바다가 이산화 탄소를 더 많이 흡수할수록 점점 더 산성이 된다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'it becomes more and more acidic' 원문 그대로. ❌ ①: Forget Me Not이 제목. ❌ ③: a year(1년). ❌ ④: dissolve(녹다)이지 harden(단단해지다)이 아님.
det.tip: Forget Me Not ≠ Remember Me. a year(1년) ≠ a month(한 달). dissolve ≠ harden.

questions.passage: Banksy's art has included environmental messages before. For example, his 2010 artwork was created at the remains of a plant in Detroit. It showed a child with a can of red paint and the words, "I remember when all this was trees." Secretive street artist Banksy designed another interesting piece of art, which appears on a concrete block garage in Port Talbot, Wales.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Banksy의 2010년 작품은 Detroit의 공장 잔해에 만들어졌다.

det.korean: 2010년 작품은 Detroit의 한 공장 잔해에 만들어졌다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 'created at the remains of a plant in Detroit' 원문 그대로. ❌ ①: Detroit이지 뉴욕이 아님. ❌ ②: secretive(비밀스러운)이지 공개적이 아님. ❌ ③: red paint(빨간색)이지 파란색이 아님.
det.tip: Detroit ≠ New York. secretive ≠ public. red ≠ blue. 세부 정보 변경 함정.

questions.passage: While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings. questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the decline of modern art in society
various techniques used in environmental photography
the economic impact of art on communities
the power of art to address environmental issues and inspire action

det.korean: 환경 문제를 다루고 행동을 촉발하는 예술의 힘.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 전문의 핵심 — 예술이 환경 문제를 다루고(addressing) 행동을 촉발(inspiring us to take action). ❌ ①: 현대 미술의 쇠퇴 — 반대. ❌ ②: 촬영 기법 — 언급 없음. ❌ ③: 경제적 영향 — 언급 없음.
det.tip: 주제는 글 전체를 관통하는 핵심 메시지. 'art + environmental issues + take action'.

questions.passage: While art can stir up a sense of beauty in us, it can also draw a spirited reaction from the public. questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: How to Become a Famous Artist
Art as a Catalyst for Environmental Change
The Scientific Approach to Solving Pollution

det.korean: 환경 변화의 촉매로서의 예술.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: catalyst(촉매) = 변화를 촉진하는 역할. 예술이 환경 변화를 이끈다는 핵심. ❌ ①: 유명 예술가 되기 — 주제 아님. ❌ ②: 환경 운동의 역사 — 역사 자체가 아님. ❌ ④: 과학적 접근 — 예술이지 과학이 아님.
det.tip: catalyst = '촉매, 촉진제'. 예술이 환경 인식과 행동 변화를 촉진한다는 의미.

questions.passage: Art can strike up conversations about the environment, but more importantly, it can also make a great difference by inspiring us to take action. The following words from Andy Warhol, an American pop artist, ring especially true in this context. "They always say time changes things, but you actually have to change them yourself."
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Andy Warhol의 인용문이 함축하는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 시간이 지나면 환경 문제는 자연스럽게 해결된다.
변화는 저절로 일어나지 않으며, 우리가 직접 행동해야 한다.

det.korean: 변화는 저절로 일어나지 않으며, 우리가 직접 행동해야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'you actually have to change them yourself' — 시간이 바꾸는 것이 아니라 본인이 직접 바꿔야 한다. ❌ ①: 자연스럽게 해결 — 정반대. ❌ ③: 예술가만 — 제한적 해석. ❌ ④: 과거와 무관 — 시간의 역할에 대한 오해.
det.tip: 'They always say time changes things, but you actually have to change them yourself' = 수동적 기다림 vs 능동적 행동.

questions.passage: The next piece, titled Forget Me Not, is Jenny Kendler's personal love letter to the sea. She covered an old boom box with various shells, which took her a year to collect. The boom box plays something you may regard as calming ocean sounds. <u>They</u> are actually what she recorded as she had one of her baby teeth dissolve in acid. She wanted us to think of what sea creatures might go through one day if we continue burning fossil fuels carelessly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 They가 가리키는 것은?
ch: the sounds from the boom box

det.korean: 카세트 플레이어에서 나오는 소리들.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 앞 문장의 'something you may regard as calming ocean sounds'를 받는 대명사. They = 그 소리들. ❌ ①: shells는 물리적 물건. ❌ ②: sea creatures는 이후에 등장. ❌ ④: fossil fuels는 다른 문맥.
det.tip: They는 앞 문장의 복수명사를 받음. 'something(calming ocean sounds)' → 'They(= those sounds)'.

Most of his work, including this painting, is a celebration of nature and a quiet appeal to humans to appreciate the world around them. "I believe we've separated ourselves from nature and no longer see how we fit in. Instead of helping nature thrive, we are simply consuming <u>it</u>," says Ching. One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which are rich in color and tenderness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것은?

det.korean: 자연이 번성하도록 돕는 대신 그저 자연을 소비하고 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: 'Instead of helping nature thrive, we are simply consuming it'. it = nature. 자연을 소비한다는 맥락. ❌ ②: 그림을 소비한다는 것은 부자연스러움. ❌ ③: 세상을 소비 — 맥락과 멀음. ❌ ④: 호소를 소비 — 비문맥적.
det.tip: it은 바로 앞의 nature를 지칭. 'helping nature thrive' → 'consuming it(= nature)'.

questions.passage: Dependence on plastic is built into the supply chain, so the individual consumer finds it harder and harder to opt out. Of course, you can choose not to purchase products containing plastic, but that only goes so far. I think it is important for you to inform your friends and family of the issue because at the end of the day, you know, companies and governments can't ignore the interest of the consumers.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Von Wong이 소비자에게 중요하다고 강조하는 행동을 본문에서 찾아 **영어** 단어로 쓰시오. (한 단어)

det.korean: 친구와 가족에게 문제를 알리다(inform).
det.analysis: 원문: 'it is important for you to inform your friends and family of the issue'. Von Wong이 소비자에게 강조하는 핵심 행동은 inform(알리다).
det.tip: inform A of B = 'A에게 B를 알리다'. Von Wong의 핵심 메시지: 주변 사람들에게 알리는 것이 중요.

questions.passage: One cannot help but smile at his paintings, which are rich in color and tenderness. One of the fun aspects of his work is how he blends the features of one life form with those of another. I've been using my work as a means of commenting on issues and problems I'm heavily interested in.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.
Jon Ching's paintings are full of color and (tend) __________.

det.korean: Jon Ching의 그림은 색감과 부드러움이 가득하다.
det.analysis: tend → tender(형용사) → tenderness(명사). 'full of + 명사' 구조이므로 명사형 tenderness가 필요.
det.tip: tend(경향이 있다, 동사) → tender(부드러운, 형용사) → tenderness(부드러움, 명사). -ness 접미사.

questions.passage: I wanted to inspire people to raise their own awareness about what they can actually do as individuals, but at the same time, I hoped to encourage collective action and collective responsibility. One thing that art can do really well is to help us imagine how the world might be otherwise. __________.
questions.stem:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
[ can't / we / certainly / get / a different place / to / if / imagine / we / it / can't ]
questions.wa: Certainly we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it
accept: Certainly we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it
certainly we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it
Certainly, we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it

det.korean: 분명 우리가 다른 곳을 상상하지 않으면, 우리는 그곳에 이를 수 없다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'Certainly, we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it.' 부사(Certainly) + 주절(we can't get to a different place) + if절(we can't imagine it).
det.tip: get to = '~에 도달하다'. if절은 조건을 나타냄. certainly = '분명, 확실히'.

questions.ans: Certainly we can't get to a different place if we can't imagine it

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 영어로 옮기시오.
뛰어난 예술 작품은 우리에게 메시지를 전해 줄 수 있고 심지어 우리가 주변을 바라보는 방식을 바꿀 수도 있다.
questions.wa: An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings.
accept: An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings.
An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change the way we look at our surroundings.
An excellent art piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings.

det.korean: 뛰어난 예술 작품은 우리에게 메시지를 전해 줄 수 있고 심지어 주변을 바라보는 방식을 바꿀 수도 있다.
det.analysis: communicate a message to us = 메시지를 전하다. change our ways of looking at = 바라보는 방식을 바꾸다. our surroundings = 우리 주변.
det.tip: ways of V-ing = '~하는 방식'. communicate = '전달하다'. surroundings = '주변 환경'.

questions.ans: An excellent artistic piece can communicate a message to us and even change our ways of looking at our surroundings.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 영어로 옮기시오.
자연을 보호하는 것은 사실 우리 자신을 보호하는 것이다.
questions.wa: Protecting nature is actually protecting us.
accept: Protecting nature is actually protecting us.
protecting nature is actually protecting us.
Protecting nature is actually protecting ourselves.
To protect nature is actually to protect us.

det.korean: 자연을 보호하는 것은 사실 우리 자신을 보호하는 것이다.
det.analysis: 동명사 주어(Protecting nature) + is + 동명사 보어(protecting us). actually = 사실은.
det.tip: 동명사 주어: V-ing + 명사 = ~하는 것은. actually = '사실은, 실제로'.

questions.ans: Protecting nature is actually protecting us.
